item.title: AI Security
item.description: <p>Two weeks ago, I attended the <a href="https://unpromptedcon.org/">[un]prompted</a> AI security conference in San Francisco. It was an excellent event: three days of very dense talks about all aspects of AI security. (My talk was about integrous AI, and I will post it when it is online.)</p> <p>AI security can be divided into three broad topics. It&#8217;s important for researchers to understand which one they are working on. And it&#8217;s important for us as a community to work on them all. They are: security of AI, security with AI, and security from AI. [un]prompted had good talks about all three...</p>
item.dc:creator: Bruce Schneier

item.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
item.description:
Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found.
The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without logging in. Zyxel has released new firmware for 10 GS1900 models that closes the hole.

item.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
item.description: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

item.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
item.description:
Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0.
Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation, the Xen Project said in an&nbsp;advisory&nbsp;on November 3.
